newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Peace coordinator bemoans Belgrade violence.
newsitem.headline: Peace coordinator bemoans Belgrade violence.

text.p: The international High Representative to former Yugoslavia, Carl Bildt, denounced Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Monday for resorting to police force against peaceful demonstrators.
Bildt urged the Serbian government to recognise the results of municipal elections.

"President Milosevic must desist from the ordering of violent repression and must definitely put aside any idea that the prolonged crisis in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia can be resolved without the honouring of electoral results," said Colum Murphy, a spokesman for the High Representative's office.
Murphy told a news conference in Sarajevo that the crisis in Belgrade and other Serbian cities could only be settled via peaceful dialogue and "honourable political compromise".
"Any attempt to resolve the crisis differently, by violence or dissembling, will meet with broad, clear and strong condemnation from the international community," he said.

Bildt, who oversees civilian aspects of the Dayton peace agreement in former Yugoslavia, has described Serbia as "the sick man of Europe" and urged European countries to take a tough line against Milosevic's handling of the crisis.
Bildt has warned that long-term stability in the Balkans will be jeopardised unless Serbia adopts fundamental political and ecoonomic reforms.
